title: A budget audio shelf

brief.decision: Which headphones and earbuds go on the new budget audio shelf, and at what price
brief.deadline: Before the shelf plan goes to the stores next week

checkpoints.prompt: Write the query that answers Sanne's question.

Sanne has a follow-up: what is the highest shelf price on the budget shelf? Look at the headphones and earbuds (category_id 15 or 16) whose unit_cost_eur is under 40.00 euros; a product with a missing unit_cost_eur does not count. A product's shelf price is its unit_cost_eur plus a 60 percent markup on it. Type the highest shelf price in euros, rounded to 2 decimals.

model_plan:
Metric formula: shelf_price_eur is unit_cost_eur plus 60 percent of it, that is unit_cost_eur times 1.6.
Output grain: one row per product.
Tables and keys: products only, keyed by product_id; no join.
Filters: category_id 15 or 16, and unit_cost_eur under 40.00; the two categories sit in brackets, because AND is worked out before OR.
Edge cases: a missing unit_cost_eur fails the cost test and drops out, and products with the same unit cost are ordered by product_id.
Expected row count: 17
model_answer_template: At a 60 percent markup, the most expensive product on the budget audio shelf would sell for {CP4} euros. The list covers two categories, and the cost cut may leave the shelf leaning on one of them, so check the category split in the result. A markup is a plan, not a market price: it says nothing yet about what shoppers will pay or what competitors charge. Next, check the shelf prices against competitor prices and last year's sales before the shelf goes live.
follow_up_question: Which of these products sold the most units last year?
